text: The LORD said to Moses:
Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
Outside the curtain of the testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall tend them before the LORD from evening until morning, continually. This is a lasting statute for your generations.
He shall keep the lamps on the pure gold lampstand burning before the LORD continually.
Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
Arrange them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
Place pure frankincense along each row, to serve as the memorial portion for the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.

versions.text: Place pure incense beside each row, to be a memorial portion with the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לְבֹנָה refers specifically to frankincense, not incense in general (which would be קְטֹרֶת). Naming it precisely preserves the distinction between the frankincense set beside the bread and the compounded incense burned on the altar.

versions.text: Place pure frankincense beside each row, to be a memorial portion with the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לַלֶּחֶם is a dative of reference: the frankincense functions as the memorial portion *for* (on behalf of) the bread, since the loaves themselves were eaten by the priests while the frankincense was burned. 'With the bread' blurs this and could suggest the bread itself was burned. Also, עַל־הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת is more naturally 'along/upon the row' than 'beside', though the sense of placement alongside is retained.

text: Sabbath after Sabbath the bread is to be set out before the LORD, continually, on behalf of the Israelites, as a lasting covenant.
It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from the offerings made to the LORD by fire—his portion forever.

versions.text: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place, for it is a most holy portion of his regular share of the offerings made to the LORD by fire—a lasting statute.
versions.explanation: The current wording piles up "a most holy portion of his regular share ... a lasting statute," which is redundant and hard to follow when read aloud. The Hebrew simply says it is most holy to him from the fire offerings, a perpetual due; the revision keeps that sense with a cleaner cadence.

text: Now the son of an Israelite woman whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse, so they brought him to Moses. (His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
They put him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
Then the LORD said to Moses:
Take the blasphemer outside the camp. All who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the whole assembly is to stone him.
Say to the Israelites: Anyone who curses his God is to bear the consequences of his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must be put to death; the whole assembly is to stone him. Foreigner and native-born alike, whoever blasphemes the Name must die.
Whoever takes a human life must be put to death.
Whoever kills an animal must make restitution for it—life for life.

versions.text: Whoever kills someone's animal must make restitution—life for life.
versions.explanation: The possessive "someone's" is not in the Hebrew (נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֵמָה, "the life of an animal") and creates an inconsistency with verse 21, which renders the same phrase as "kills an animal."

text: Whoever injures his neighbor is to receive the same injury in return:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has injured another, so is he to be injured.
Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a human being must be put to death.
You are to have the same law for the foreigner as for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.
Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
